purpose: Layer 3b of citation accuracy - IS THE CITED PARAGRAPH THE RIGHT ONE? align.py chooses the paragraph, so it cannot grade its own choice; this set is hand-graded against the parsed documents and reported as a SAMPLE, never as a rate.
rules_this_set_follows: NEW questions. None appears in the 48-question golden set, so the aligner has not been tuned against them.

SINGLE-SOURCE. Each question is written so a correct answer should rest on ONE paragraph per claim. Cross-section questions are excluded on purpose: when a claim legitimately draws on three paragraphs, 'which paragraph did it come from' has no single right answer and the grade becomes an opinion.
ONE OR MORE PER PLAN MODE, so a failure can be attributed to a shape of question rather than to the corpus at large.

NOT VERIFIED AGAINST THE CORPUS. These are written from the registry's subject/jurisdiction labels, not from reading the documents. Anuj validates before use - any question whose answer turns out to span sections should be dropped, not graded.
how_to_grade: 1. Run the question. Record each claim, its label, and the locator align.py assigned.
2. Open the delivered window (the passage text) and read its paragraphs.
3. For each claim, decide by hand which paragraph the sentence actually came from.
4. Mark RIGHT / WRONG / UNGRADABLE. UNGRADABLE is not a failure - it means the claim drew on more than one paragraph, and that question should leave the set.
5. Report as 'n of m claims correctly located, hand-graded', with the misses quoted. Never as a percentage of the corpus.

questions.question: What does BCBS 239 require of a bank's data architecture and IT infrastructure?
questions.why_this_one: A named document with a numbered principle - the cleanest possible single-paragraph target.

questions.question: What does SS1/23 say about the responsibilities of the board for model risk?
questions.why_this_one: UK side of MRM, named document, and the only UK document in the corpus - no jurisdiction ambiguity to confound the grade.

questions.question: What does Basel LEX define as a large exposure?
questions.why_this_one: A definition. Definitions live in one paragraph, which is exactly the shape 3b needs.

questions.question: What does 12 CFR 225.8 require a bank holding company to include in its capital plan?
questions.why_this_one: US rule text, named. Rule text is enumerated, so a claim that wanders between items is visible to a hand grader.

questions.question: What does SR 11-7 say about the independence of model validation?
questions.why_this_one: The corpus's only superseded document. Worth one question on its own: a citation into a historic document must still locate correctly.

questions.question: What does IFRS 9 require when measuring expected credit losses at initial recognition?
questions.why_this_one: IFRS 9 is the parent that produced empty containers in an earlier defect - a locator failure here would be informative twice over.

questions.question: What do UK supervisory expectations require for the independence of model validation?
questions.why_this_one: No document named, one jurisdiction. Tests whether the locator survives when the planner, not the sentence, picked the document.

questions.question: What must a US firm submit to the Federal Reserve as part of its annual stress test?
questions.why_this_one: The crowded US stress-testing cell - six documents. If a locator is going to point into the wrong window, this is where.

questions.question: What do UK and US expectations each say about who owns a model?
questions.why_this_one: Two facets, one claim per side. Each claim should still rest on one paragraph, so 3b is gradable even though the answer is not single-source overall.

questions.question: How do UK and US expectations each define a model?
questions.why_this_one: A definition on both sides - the fan-out equivalent of cb-03, and the strongest single-paragraph target this mode allows.

questions.question: What changed in US model risk guidance compared with the previous version?
questions.why_this_one: The only version pair the corpus holds (SR 26-2 against SR 11-7). A change claim must locate in BOTH windows, which is two grades from one question.

questions.question: What do Basel CAP and Basel RBC each say about the composition of Tier 1 capital?
questions.why_this_one: Two named documents, one search each. Tests that a locator is taken from the right document's window, not merely the right paragraph number.

questions.question: What is effective challenge in model risk management?
questions.why_this_one: Subject only - no document, no jurisdiction. The rule-6 fan-out that sat dead until 2026-09-09; its citations have never been located by hand.

questions.question: What is a significant increase in credit risk?
questions.why_this_one: Subject only, and a term of art with a definition - so the right paragraph is decidable by a reader who is not a credit specialist.

questions.question: What does Basel SRP32 say about the governance of a bank's internal stress testing programme?
questions.why_this_one: A global stress-testing document, to check that the crowded US cell in cb-08 is a jurisdiction problem and not a subject problem.
